related_questions.question: Is there a cure for HMPV?
related_questions.snippet: As hMPV is a cold virus, people can treat their symptoms with over-the-counter medicines to treat pain, fever, stuffy nose and cough. Getting plenty of rest and staying hydrated also helps. Currently, there is no approved antiviral medicine for hMPV. Most people feel better in a few days.

related_questions.question: How long is someone contagious with HMPV?
related_questions.snippet: How long can I spread the virus to others? You can infect others for 1-2 weeks, but you can be contagious for weeks or even months if you have a weakened immune system. The time period from when a person is exposed to human metapneumovirus and when they begin to develop symptoms is 3-7 days.

text_blocks.snippet: HMPV, or human metapneumovirus, starts with exposure to the virus, typically through respiratory droplets released when an infected person coughs or sneezes, or by touching contaminated surfaces and then touching your face. The virus then enters the body through the nose, mouth, or eyes.
snippet_highlighted_words: starts with exposure to the virus, typically through respiratory droplets released when an infected person coughs or sneezes, or by touching contaminated surfaces and then touching your face

list.title: Transmission:
list.snippet: HMPV spreads through close contact with an infected person or by touching contaminated surfaces.

list.title: Respiratory Droplets:
list.snippet: When an infected person coughs or sneezes, they release tiny droplets containing the virus into the air. These droplets can be inhaled by others nearby or land on surfaces.

list.title: Contaminated Surfaces:
list.snippet: The virus can survive on surfaces for a short period. If you touch a contaminated surface and then touch your face (eyes, nose, or mouth), you can become infected.

list.title: Incubation Period:
list.snippet: After exposure, it typically takes 3 to 6 days for symptoms to appear.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: HMPV symptoms are usually mild and similar to a common cold, including cough, runny nose, and fever. However, some individuals, especially young children, older adults, and those with weakened immune systems, may experience more severe illness, such as pneumonia or bronchitis.

text_blocks.snippet: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infection is a common respiratory illness, primarily affecting young children and older adults, but can impact people of all ages. It is a virus that can cause mild to severe respiratory symptoms. hMPV is spread through respiratory secretions and contaminated objects.
snippet_highlighted_words: a common respiratory illness, primarily affecting young children and older adults, but can impact people of all ages

list.snippet: Mild: Cough, runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, and fever are common.
More Severe: Wheezing, difficulty breathing, pneumonia, and worsening of asthma can occur.
hMPV is spread through close contact with respiratory secretions (coughing, sneezing) and contaminated surfaces.
It is contagious for 1-2 weeks, but individuals with weakened immune systems can be contagious for weeks or months.
The incubation period (time from exposure to symptom onset) is typically 3-7 days.
Young children, older adults, and individuals with weakened immune systems are more susceptible to severe illness.
Chronic lung conditions (like COPD or asthma) can also increase the risk of complications.
Good hygiene practices, such as frequent handwashing and covering coughs and sneezes, are important.
Avoiding close contact with sick individuals can also help reduce transmission.
Most cases are mild and resolve on their own within a week or two.
There is no specific antiviral treatment for hMPV, so treatment is usually supportive, focusing on symptom relief.
If symptoms are severe or persistent, medical advice should be sought.
